products.summary: A pen-shaped, corded ultrasonic cutter from a resin-printer maker, built to cut supports off resin prints without snapping fine parts. At $100 it costs less than the cordless rivals, and replacement blades cost about 50 cents each.
products.fit: Resin printers who print miniatures, busts or other delicate parts and break them with flush cutters, and who work at a desk near an outlet.
caveats: Corded: you work within the cord's reach of an outlet.
On PLA and other FDM plastics, friction heat can melt the cut instead of slicing it. One owner called PLA "almost impossible"; ABS and ASA worked.
Two retail owners reported a unit that died early (one within seconds). Phrozen replaced one of them.
One owner said thin supports didn't cut until they pushed hard. Hackster's reviewer found a light touch cut even thick supports.
Humans can't hear the vibration, but one reviewer's dog was upset by it.
The blade gets hot enough to burn. Let it cool before changing it.

products.returns: Not confirmed on 2026-11-11; check the Phrozen US store policy before buying
products.summary: Spare blades for the Sonic Saber. At the current price, each blade costs about 50 cents.
products.fit: Sonic Saber owners whose blade has dulled or chipped.
caveats: Fits only the Sonic Saber. It doesn't take standard hobby or snap-off blades.
Unplug the cutter and let the blade cool before swapping.

products.summary: A compact 8K resin printer with 22 µm pixels, sized for miniatures and small busts.
products.fit: Tabletop and miniature printers who want fine detail on a small footprint and don't need a large build plate.
caveats: The 6.5 × 2.8 in plate is small. Batch printing or large busts need a 10-inch or 15-inch printer.
It has a single linear rail; the older Sonic Mini 8K used dual rails.
The LCD is a consumable. A replacement screen costs $90 at Phrozen (2026-11-11).

notes:
Why this query: Phrozen's printers face crowded comparisons (Elegoo and Anycubic 12K–16K printers beat the Sonic Mini 8K S and Mighty 16K on price per resolution). Results for 'ultrasonic cutter for resin prints' are thin: maker pages, deal sites, one Hackster mini review and NeoBlade reviews. The Sonic Saber dropped from a $259.99 launch price (Hackster) to $100, which makes it the cheapest name-brand cutter for this job.

Pain points, counted across reviews, retail reviews and forums: melting or smearing on PLA/FDM plastics 6; early unit failure 5 (2 replaced under warranty); slow cutting or heavy pressure needed 3; cord vs battery 3; bulky body 3; noise bothering pets or people 2; continuous-use or thermal shutoff 2.

Winners by segment: resin supports on a budget at a desk: Phrozen Sonic Saber ($100, corded, blades about 50¢ each). Cordless or mixed materials: HOZO NeoBlade ($149; no earning route, linked to the maker page). Heavy shop use: WonderCutter X ($799.95 preorder at Micro-Mark).

Verified 2026-11-11 with storecheck: Sonic Saber $100, in stock. Blade kit $10 (compare-at $20), 20 blades, 18×4×0.38 mm, 30° tip. Sonic Mini 8K S $270, in stock, specs from the store text. NeoBlade $149 and Creator Combo $218 at HOZO. NeoBlade $149.99 preorder at Micro-Mark, with box contents and 124 g / 190 g weight. WonderCutter X $799.95 preorder, 48 W. The WonderCutter S doesn't appear in Micro-Mark's current results.

Not verified, kept off the page: the Sonic Saber's frequency (Phrozen says 'over 35,000 per second'; resellers say 40 kHz or 35 kHz); its 12 V 3 A adapter and 1 m cable (resellers only); its '5 consecutive minutes' limit and orange overheat light (Filament2Print listing only, Phrozen's manual unreadable); Phrozen warranty length and return policy (Phrozen product and policy pages returned HTTP 429 all session; storecheck search worked, but product calls and WebFetch did not); the contents of the 'Sonic Saber Bundle-Black Friday 2026' ($80, compare-at $128, seen in store search 2026-11-11).
